greeting.text: Margaret Vale speaking. What would you like to ask?

fallback.speaker: Margaret Vale
fallback.text: I cannot connect those details. Ask me about Edward, the messages or his papers.

greeting.speaker: Leo Mercer
greeting.text: Mercer Audio. We preserve memories. We do not improve the singing. What is your enquiry?

fallback.speaker: Leo Mercer
fallback.text: I can discuss our work, but private records require the client’s permission and a relevant enquiry.

greeting.speaker: Colin Ward
greeting.text: Ward Consulting. Clear answers, flexible invoicing. What is this about?

fallback.speaker: Colin Ward
fallback.text: I cannot give you a useful answer from those details. Be specific about the archive or company records.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Tell me about Edward and the material he left behind.

lines.speaker: Margaret Vale
lines.text: Edward died a year ago. I identified him, and I have the death certificate. I am not asking you to hold a seance.

lines.speaker: Margaret Vale
lines.text: He left older recordings: voicemail messages and notes from an office recorder. He kept so many blue folders that he could have registered as weather.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Did you speak to the caller?

lines.speaker: Margaret Vale
lines.text: All three recent calls went to voicemail, at 20:14 on successive evenings. The number was withheld. I never spoke live to the caller.

lines.speaker: Margaret Vale
lines.text: I have preserved the original files and older recordings of Edward. His voice alone does not tell me who placed a call.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: May I have copies of the older recordings?

lines.speaker: Margaret Vale
lines.text: Yes. I will supply copies of three older recordings: a blue-folder voicemail, an office recorder test and an anniversary message. I will keep the originals.

lines.speaker: Margaret Vale
lines.text: They predate Edward’s death according to my records. Compare them with the new messages before deciding what they mean.

lines.speaker: Margaret Vale
lines.text: I checked the study. The blue folder contains Edward’s reconciliation sheet, a company bank entry and Colin Ward’s earlier request for the annotated original.

lines.speaker: Margaret Vale
lines.text: The sheet records an unresolved expense claim, CW-41, linked to payment TR-884. I will send scans and keep the originals.

lines.speaker: Margaret Vale

lines.speaker: Colin Ward
lines.text: Yes. I assembled the three messages from Edward’s old recordings and sent them through my business voice-message relay. I scheduled all three for 20:14.

lines.speaker: Colin Ward
lines.text: Margaret had ignored my request for the original reconciliation sheet. I wanted Edward’s annotations out of her hands before anyone checked my expense claim. I thought his voice would make her listen.
